items.title: Niraparib Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Phase 2 Trial
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with other therapies in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine safe dosing and assess effectiveness of different drug combinations. It is no longer recruiting new patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA-617 Phase 2 Trial in Chinese Patients Completed
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial studied Lu-177 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in Chinese men with progressive PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who had previously received hormone therapy and chemotherapy. The study assessed safety, effectiveness, and drug levels to support registration in China, bridging data from the global VISION trial.

items.title: Vitamin D Replacement Study in African American Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This early phase trial examines vitamin D insufficiency rates in African American men with localized or metastatic prostate cancer and studies how vitamin D affects immune function. Researchers aim to determine if vitamin D replacement can normalize immune response, potentially impacting cancer aggressiveness.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA-617 Phase 3 Trial Recruiting for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares Ac-225 PSMA-617 (a newer radioligand) plus hormone therapy versus standard treatments in men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Eligible patients must have progressed on hormone therapy but not yet received chemotherapy or PSMA radioligand treatment. The study is actively recruiting.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA-617 Phase 3 Trial for Hormone-Sensitive Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial (1,144 patients enrolled) evaluates Lu-177 PSMA-617 combined with standard hormone therapy versus hormone therapy alone in men with newly metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting but continues following participants for outcomes.

items.title: QLC5508 Phase 3 Trial Versus Chemotherapy for mCRPC Not Yet Recruiting
items.summary: This upcoming phase 3 trial will compare QLC5508 (an investigational drug) to docetaxel chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after hormone therapy. The study aims to measure progression-free survival and will begin recruiting soon.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA-617 Combination Phase 1 Trial Suspended
items.summary: This dose-finding phase 1 trial was testing cabozantinib combined with Lu-177 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aimed to identify safe dosing but is currently suspended.

items.title: Radium-223 Versus Hormone Therapy Phase 4 Trial for Bone Metastases
items.summary: This phase 4 trial compares radium-223 (Xofigo) to switching hormone therapy in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bones after progressing on one hormone therapy. The study is no longer recruiting and aims to compare effectiveness and safety of both approaches.

items.title: Apalutamide Phase 3 Trial for Non-Metastatic Castration-Resistant Disease
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluated apalutamide in men with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting but continues following participants. This represents disease before metastases develop.

items.title: ARX517 Phase 1 Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early phase 1 trial tests ARX517 (a novel T-cell redirecting therapy) alone or in combination in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting and focuses on safety and tolerability assessment.

items.title: Mevrometostat for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Phase 1 Trial Recruiting
items.summary: This phase 1 trial studies mevrometostat (an epigenetic drug) alone and with enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after prior treatment. The study is actively recruiting to evaluate safety and effectiveness.

items.title: Pasritamig Combination Therapy Phase 1 Trial Recruiting for Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests pasritamig (a T-cell redirecting therapy targeting PSMA) alone and in combinations for metastatic prostate cancer. The study aims to identify safe dosing and is actively recruiting participants.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Hormone Therapy Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Disease
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluated whether adding apalutamide to standard hormone therapy improves survival in men with newly metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting but continues following participants for long-term outcomes.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 Trial Recruiting for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't yet received enzalutamide or abiraterone. The study is actively recruiting and aims to determine if the combination is more effective.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Gene-Mutated Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This phase 3 trial studied niraparib (PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone versus abiraterone alone in men with newly metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have specific DNA repair gene mutations. The study is no longer recruiting and targets patients with HRR gene defects.

items.title: Cabozantinib and Atezolizumab Phase 2 Trial Recruiting for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether cabozantinib (targets tumor blood vessels) combined with atezolizumab (immunotherapy) can shrink tumors in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is actively recruiting participants.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluated niraparib (PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone versus abiraterone plus placebo in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting and assessed effectiveness of the combination therapy.

items.title: Radium-223 Combinations with DNA Repair Inhibitor and Immunotherapy Trial Recruiting
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial compares radium-223 alone versus combined with M3814 (DNA repair inhibitor) and/or avelumab (immunotherapy) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases. The study is recruiting to find the best combination approach.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Chemotherapy-Naive mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compared apalutamide plus abiraterone combination versus abiraterone alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy. The study is no longer recruiting and measured time to cancer progression.

items.title: IL-12 Enhanced Human PSMA-CAR T Cell Therapy Development for Advanced Disease
items.summary: Researchers developed an improved CAR T-cell therapy targeting PSMA in advanced prostate cancer. The therapy uses human-derived antibody components and includes IL-12 to enhance T-cell function, showing promising tumor-killing ability in laboratory studies with better safety profile than previous versions.

items.title: 2025 Advances in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer Review
items.summary: This review summarizes major 2025 developments in radioactive drug treatments for prostate cancer. The field has expanded from radium-223 for bone pain to PSMA-targeted therapies that directly treat cancer, representing significant progress in treatment options for advanced disease.

items.title: Optimizing Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Guidelines
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This educational article provides a practical framework for managing metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It integrates clinical features, molecular testing, imaging, and supportive care to guide treatment decisions, addressing the complexity of sequencing multiple available therapies including hormone blockers, chemotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and radioactive treatments.

items.title: Novel Therapies Beyond Androgen Blockade for mCRPC Review
items.summary: This review discusses emerging treatment strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer beyond hormone therapy. It covers PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, metabolic therapies, PSMA radioligand therapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and bispecific antibodies, highlighting how understanding tumor biology drives new treatment development.

items.title: Prognostic Factors for PSMA Radioligand Therapy in mCRPC Meta-Analysis
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of multiple studies identified factors that predict outcomes for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer receiving PSMA radioligand therapy. Understanding these prognostic factors helps clinicians identify which patients are most likely to benefit from this treatment.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Drug Resistance in mCRPC Research
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT pathways to overcome resistance to AKT inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This dual-target approach addresses c-MYC-driven resistance that limits effectiveness of single-drug treatments.

items.title: Emerging Theranostic Targets Beyond PSMA for Prostate Cancer Review
items.summary: This review explores alternative molecular targets for radioactive drug treatments in prostate cancer beyond PSMA. It discusses multiple promising biomarkers that could help treat tumors with low PSMA expression or expand treatment options, potentially benefiting patients who don't respond to current PSMA-targeted therapies.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in mCRPC Meta-Analysis Shows Mixed Results
items.summary: This analysis of 1,580 patients from 21 trials evaluated immune checkpoint inhibitor effectiveness in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Results show combination therapies with immunotherapy demonstrated some benefit compared to single-drug approaches, but outcomes varied, suggesting patient selection is important.
